## Managed Agents (Beta)

**Managed Agents** is a third surface: server-managed stateful agents with Anthropic-hosted tool execution. You create a persisted, versioned Agent config (`POST /v1/agents`), then start Sessions that reference it. Each session provisions a container as the agent's workspace - bash, file ops, and code execution run there; the agent loop itself runs on Anthropic's orchestration layer and acts on the container via tools. The session streams events; you send messages and tool results back.

Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. For agents on Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry (where Managed Agents is unsupported), use Claude API + tool use.

**Mandatory flow:** Agent (once) -> Session (every run). `model`/`system`/`tools` live on the agent, never the session. See `shared/managed-agents-overview.md` for the full reading guide, beta headers, and pitfalls.

**Beta headers:** `managed-agents-2026-04-01` - the SDK sets this automatically for all `client.beta.{agents,environments,sessions,vaults,deployments,deployment_runs}.*` calls. Memory stores use `agent-memory-2026-07-22` instead, which the SDK sets on `client.beta.memory_stores.*` calls; sending both headers on a memory store request returns a 400. Files API and Skills API are out of beta - no beta header needed (see the API Drift table above for the migration guides).

**Subcommands** - invoke directly with `/claude-api <subcommand>`:

| Subcommand | Action |
|---|---|
| `managed-agents-onboard` | Walk the user through setting up a Managed Agent from scratch. **Read `shared/managed-agents-onboarding.md` immediately** and follow its interview script: **describe -> configure the agent (propose, don't interrogate) -> environment -> session** (same arc as the Console quickstart, auth deferred to the session step) - defaults and inline suggestions do the work, with a silent viability gate (job vs tools/credentials/data) before any code is emitted. Do not summarize - run the interview. |

**Reading guide:** Start with `shared/managed-agents-overview.md`, then the topical `shared/managed-agents-*.md` files (core, environments, tools, events, outcomes, multiagent, webhooks, memory, scheduled-deployments, client-patterns, onboarding, api-reference). For Python, TypeScript, Go, Ruby, PHP, and Java, read `{lang}/managed-agents/README.md` for code examples. For cURL, read `curl/managed-agents.md`. **Agents are persistent - create once, reference by ID.** Define agents and environments as version-controlled files synced with `ant apply` - this is the recommended flow (see `shared/anthropic-cli.md`): the CLI owns the control plane (creating and updating agents), your code owns the data plane (`sessions.create` with the stored agent ID). Call `agents.create()` in code only when you must provision programmatically; either way, store the returned agent ID and pass it to every subsequent `sessions.create`; never call `agents.create()` in the request path. If a binding you need isn't shown in the language README, WebFetch the relevant entry from `shared/live-sources.md` rather than guess. C# has beta Managed Agents support via `client.Beta.Agents` and related namespaces - see `csharp/claude-api/README.md` for details, or `curl/managed-agents.md` for raw HTTP reference.

**When the user wants to set up a Managed Agent from scratch** (e.g. "how do I get started", "walk me through creating one", "set up a new agent"): read `shared/managed-agents-onboarding.md` and run its interview - same flow as the `managed-agents-onboard` subcommand.

**When the user asks "how do I write the client code for X":** reach for `shared/managed-agents-client-patterns.md` - covers lossless stream reconnect, `processed_at` queued/processed gate, interrupt, `tool_confirmation` round-trip, the correct idle/terminated break gate, post-idle status race, stream-first ordering, file-mount gotchas, etc. For credentials, lead with vault `environment_variable` credentials - the first-class mechanism; secrets are substituted at egress and never enter the sandbox (`shared/managed-agents-tools.md` -> Vaults). Keeping credentials host-side via custom tools is the fallback where vault credentials don't fit (e.g. self-hosted sandboxes).

**When the task is a deliverable - default the kickoff to an outcome, not a plain message.** If the session's job is to produce something checkable (an artifact, a report, a PR, a dataset, a fixed set of changes), read `shared/managed-agents-outcomes.md` and kick off with `user.define_outcome` plus a starter rubric you draft from the task (5-10 concrete, independently gradeable criteria; comment it as a starter to tune). Reserve plain `user.message` for genuinely conversational sessions. Trigger on intent, not just the word: "keep working until it's right", "make sure the output is actually good", "don't stop at a first draft" all mean outcomes.

**When the user asks about tool approvals, permission policies, or "auto mode"** (which tool calls need a human, letting the server evaluate calls, `evaluated_permission` / `evaluation` on tool-use events): read `shared/managed-agents-tools.md` § Permission Policies - `always_allow` / `always_ask` / `auto` and the three `auto` outcomes (runs, denied as high-risk, pauses when indeterminate). For attaching a terminal to a live session (`ant beta:sessions connect`): `shared/anthropic-cli.md`.

**When the user wants the agent to run on a schedule** (cron, "every night", "weekly report"): read `shared/managed-agents-scheduled-deployments.md` - deployments fire sessions autonomously on a cron cadence, with per-firing run records and lifecycle controls (pause/unpause/archive).

**When the agent's work fans out** (research across several sources, per-file or per-record work, "look into N things, then summarize") **or one loop would fill its context with reading:** read `shared/managed-agents-multiagent.md` and recommend a multiagent session - start with just `{"type": "self"}` in the roster so the agent can delegate to copies of itself, then move reading-heavy sub-tasks to a cheaper worker agent (e.g. Claude Haiku 4.5, or Claude Sonnet 5.5 when the worker needs more judgment) referenced by ID.

## Server Tools (Quick Reference)

Server-side tools run on Anthropic's infrastructure - no client-side execution loop. Declare in `tools`; results arrive as content blocks in the same response. **No beta header** unless noted. **Prefer the latest type variant your model supports.** The `_20260209` web search / web fetch variants below (dynamic filtering) require Opus 5.5/5/4.8/4.7/4.6, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, or Sonnet 4.6; the basic variants for older models are listed after the table.

| Tool | `type` | `name` | Key optional params | Result block type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Web search | `web_search_20260209` | `web_search` | `max_uses`, `allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains`, `user_location` | `web_search_tool_result` -> `.content` is a list of `web_search_result` |
| Web fetch | `web_fetch_20260209` | `web_fetch` | `max_uses`, `allowed_domains`/`blocked_domains`, `citations`, `max_content_tokens` | `web_fetch_tool_result` -> `.content` is a `web_fetch_result` with a `document` block |
| Code execution | `code_execution_20260521` | `code_execution` | none | `bash_code_execution_tool_result` -> `.content.stdout` / `.stderr` / `.return_code` |
| Tool search (regex) | `tool_search_tool_regex_20251119` | `tool_search_tool_regex` | mark other tools `defer_loading: true` | `tool_search_tool_result` |
| Tool search (BM25) | `tool_search_tool_bm25_20251119` | `tool_search_tool_bm25` | mark other tools `defer_loading: true` | `tool_search_tool_result` |

`web_search_20260209` / `web_fetch_20260209` have built-in dynamic filtering - code execution runs under the hood, so do **not** separately declare `code_execution` in `tools` (a second execution environment confuses the model). For models older than Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6, use the basic variants `web_search_20250305` / `web_fetch_20250910` instead; on Vertex AI only basic `web_search_20250305` is available. `code_execution_20260120` (REPL persistence + programmatic tool calling) runs on Opus 4.5+ / Sonnet 4.5+. **Go SDK only**: `code_execution_20260521` lives under `client.Beta.Messages.New` with `Betas: []anthropic.AnthropicBeta{"code-execution-2025-08-25"}` (other languages use plain `client.messages.create`); `code_execution_20260120` uses the non-beta `client.Messages.New` in Go like everywhere else. Web fetch only fetches URLs already present in the conversation. Provider availability varies by tool - see `shared/platform-availability.md`. See `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` for `pause_turn` handling.

## Document & File Input (Quick Reference)

**PDF (base64, no beta):** `{"type": "document", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "application/pdf", "data": <b64 string>}}` in user content, placed before the text block. Base64 string must have no newlines. Limits: 32 MB request, 600 pages (100 for 200k-context models). Java: `ContentBlockParam.ofDocument(DocumentBlockParam... Base64PdfSource.builder().data(...))`.

**Files API (no beta):** upload via `client.files.upload(...)` -> response `id` is the `file_id`. Reference it as `{"type": "document", "source": {"type": "file", "file_id": "..."}}` for PDF/text, or `{"type": "image", ...}` for images - the content-block type must match the file's MIME type. To migrate code off `files-api-2025-04-14`, WebFetch the Files API row in `shared/live-sources.md`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.

**Citations (no beta):** set `citations: {enabled: true}` on each `document` content block (all or none). Response splits into multiple `text` blocks; cited blocks carry a `citations` array. Each citation has `cited_text`, `document_index`, `document_title`, and a location by `type`: `char_location` (`start_char_index`/`end_char_index`) for plain text, `page_location` (`start_page_number`/`end_page_number`, 1-indexed) for PDF, `content_block_location` for custom content. Incompatible with `output_config.format` (returns a 400).

## Tool Use Patterns (Quick Reference)

**Strict tool use (no beta):** set `strict: true` as a top-level field on the tool definition (alongside `name`/`description`/`input_schema`), **not** on `tool_choice`. Schema must have `additionalProperties: false` + `required`. Guarantees `tool_use.input` validates exactly. Go: `Strict: anthropic.Bool(true)` + `additionalProperties` via `InputSchema.ExtraFields`; Java: `.strict(true)` + `.putAdditionalProperty("additionalProperties", JsonValue.from(false))`.

**Parallel tool use (default on):** one assistant message may contain multiple `tool_use` blocks. Execute them concurrently, then return **all** `tool_result` blocks in a **single** user message - splitting them across multiple messages silently trains Claude to stop making parallel calls. For a failed tool, return `tool_result` with `is_error: true` - don't drop it.

**Tool Runner (SDK beta helper):** drives the tool-call loop for you via `client.beta.messages.*`. Python: `@beta_tool` decorator + `client.beta.messages.tool_runner(...)` -> `runner.until_done()`. TypeScript: `betaZodTool({...})` from `@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/beta/zod` + `client.beta.messages.toolRunner(...)` -> `await runner`. Go: `toolrunner.NewBetaToolFromJSONSchema(...)` + `client.Beta.Messages.NewToolRunner(...)` -> `.RunToCompletion(ctx)`. Java requires `.addBeta("structured-outputs-2025-11-13")`. Ruby: `Anthropic::BaseTool` subclass + `client.beta.messages.tool_runner(...)`. PHP: `BetaRunnableTool` + `->toolRunner(...)`. C#: raw JSON-schema tools + `BetaToolRunner` via `client.Beta.Messages.ToolRunner(...)`.

**Programmatic tool calling (no beta header):** Claude calls your custom tool from inside code execution. Add `{"type": "code_execution_20260120", "name": "code_execution"}` **and** set `"allowed_callers": ["code_execution_20260120"]` on your custom tool. Opus 4.5+ / Sonnet 4.5+ (availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`). When responding to a pending programmatic call, the user message must contain **only** `tool_result` blocks (no text). Not compatible with `strict: true`, `disable_parallel_tool_use`, forced `tool_choice`, or MCP tools.

## Other API Surfaces (Quick Reference)

**Message Batches (no beta; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`):** `client.messages.batches.create(requests=[{custom_id, params}, ...])` -> poll `client.messages.batches.retrieve(id).processing_status` until `"ended"` -> stream `client.messages.batches.results(id)`. Each result has `.custom_id` + `.result.type` (`succeeded`/`errored`/`canceled`/`expired`); on success read `.result.message.content`. Python wraps requests as `Request(custom_id=..., params=MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming(...))`. Results arrive in **any order** - key by `custom_id`, never by position.

**Models API (no beta; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`):** `client.models.list()` (auto-paginates) and `client.models.retrieve("claude-opus-5-5")`. Each model object has `id`, `display_name`, `created_at`, and - since Mar 2026 - `max_input_tokens` (the context window), `max_tokens` (the output cap), and `capabilities`. There is no `context_window` field.

**Stop details (GA, Opus 4.7+):** `response.stop_details` is populated **only when `stop_reason == "refusal"`** (fields: `type: "refusal"`, `category` - an open set, e.g. `"cyber"`, `"bio"`, `"reasoning_extraction"`, `"frontier_llm"`, or `null`; see the docs for the full list - and `explanation`). It is `null` for every other `stop_reason` (`end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `tool_use`, `pause_turn`, ...) - always guard before reading.

**Admin API (beta, since 2026-08-26):** organization management - members, invites, workspaces and workspace members, API keys, rate limit reports, service accounts, federation issuers/rules, CMEK external keys - under `client.beta.organization` in all seven SDKs and `ant beta:organization` in the CLI. Requires an admin credential: an Admin API key (`sk-ant-admin...`, read from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) or an `org:admin` OAuth token (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`); regular API keys are rejected. Usage and cost reports and the Claude Enterprise user-management/analytics endpoints are **not** in the SDKs - raw HTTP only. See `shared/admin-api.md`.

**Client config (no beta):** `timeout` default 10 min; **units differ by SDK** - Python/Ruby: seconds; TypeScript: **milliseconds**; Go `option.WithRequestTimeout(time.Duration)`; Java `Duration`; C# `TimeSpan`. TS scales the default up to 60 min for large `max_tokens` on non-streaming requests; Java does so for streaming requests (Java non-streaming scales 30s-10 min). `max_retries`/`maxRetries` default 2 (retries 408/409/429/5xx + connection errors). `base_url` (or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env). Per-request override: Python `client.with_options(timeout=5.0).messages.create(...)`; TS `client.messages.create({...}, {timeout: 5_000})`; Ruby `request_options: {timeout: 5}`. Timeouts are retried - wall-clock can reach `timeout × (max_retries+1)`.

## Workload Identity Federation (Quick Reference)

**GA, no beta header.** Construct the normal zero-arg client (`Anthropic()` / `new Anthropic()` / `anthropic.NewClient()` / `AnthropicOkHttpClient.fromEnv()`); the SDK auto-detects WIF when **all** of `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `ANTHROPIC_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID`, and `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` (or `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN`) are set, exchanges the JWT at `/v1/oauth/token`, and auto-refreshes. `ANTHROPIC_WORKSPACE_ID` does not gate activation - required only when the federation rule spans multiple workspaces (else 400 `workspace_id_required`), optional for single-workspace rules. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (even empty) outrank WIF, and a set `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` also wins over the federation env vars (a missing named profile is an error, not a fall-through) - unset all three.

## When to Use WebFetch

Use WebFetch to get the latest documentation when:

- User asks for "latest" or "current" information
- Cached data seems incorrect
- User asks about features not covered here

Live documentation URLs are in `shared/live-sources.md`.

## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim - when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** - the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** - they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` - hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` -> Pre-warming).

I'm planning out the module structure next: a typed vocab loader and text utilities for tokenizing and humanizing, followed by the staged pipeline files (quality, suitability, glb, wav, dedupe, filters), storage and tooling layers, and the provider bridge. Starting with the vocab loader implementation now.

For tokenizePath I'm working through splitting directories and filenames, handling camelCase and digit boundaries, stripping extensions, parsing comma-separated tags, and normalizing to lowercase synonyms. For deciding whether a word counts as "content," I'm leaning toward requiring it to appear in a known vocabulary set (keywords, tags, taxonomy words) rather than relying on an external dictionary, so coverage stays honest and strict, checking whether a system word list might be available to supplement this.

I'm sketching the RawAsset input shape with fields like id, source, pack, path, kind, licensing, and measurement data, plus optional side metadata and per-pack info, which Stage A will validate into a CatalogEntry with coverage. For titles, I'm defining the logic to prefer an existing name field, humanizing it while preserving variant numbers, and falling back to humanizing filename tokens when no name is present.

Now I'm working out the fallback case where filenames yield no usable words, combining pack title, folder words, and the trailing number instead. I'm also drafting kind-specific short description templates—models get a style/noun/category phrase with triangle count and source pack, texture sets get resolution and map-type details, and sounds get a tone/duration description—favoring my own consistent generation over sometimes awkward existing descriptions, truncated to 140 characters.

For category assignment, I'm laying out a priority order: raw category alias first, then side category/subcategory, then a keyword vote across filename, folder, and pack tokens weighted by source and restricted to domains appropriate for each asset kind (objects for models/sprites/decals, materials for textures, environment for HDRIs, sound/music domains for audio), with secondary candidates reported if their score clears a threshold or conflicts with the alias.

For tags, I'm planning a union of raw tags, side tags, filename/folder tokens, and theme-relevant pack name words, canonicalized and then split into controlled tags (matching known vocab/style/category keyword sets) versus free tags (capped at 8, filtering out numbers and generic words), plus kind-specific tags like tileable, pbr, animated, rigged, loopable, or transient based on asset properties. For style, I'm deriving it from style keywords matched against tags, pack name, and side styles, with source-based fallbacks like Kenney 3D defaulting to "low-poly" unless I decide against guessing without evidence.

I'm building a deterministic source-to-style mapping table since sources like Quaternius and KayKit are consistently low-poly/stylized while Polyhaven and ambientCG are photorealistic scans, so I'll add this as a "sourceStyles" lookup in the vocab, leaving ambiguous sources like basemesh libraries unmapped. Then I'm outlining the quality-check rules for model assets, scoring things like glb format, known triangle counts against budget thresholds, file size limits, bounding box scale, material presence, thumbnail existence, and documented licensing with weighted penalties for each.

For texture sets I'm checking that core PBR maps (albedo, normal, roughness) exist, resolution meets a 1024px floor, normal map convention is known, physical size is specified, and licensing/thumbnail info is present. For single textures, sprites, and decals I'm checking known dimensions, power-of-two sizing, a 4096px ceiling, licensing, and a minimum size floor to flag anything too tiny. For HDRIs I'm checking resolution floor, correct hdr/exr format, and licensing, and for audio I'm defining checks spanning decode success, duration ranges, true peak and clipping limits, silence ratio, DC offset, sample rate floor, loudness floor, and licensing.

I'm computing the final score as a weighted average of measured checks scaled by how much of the total was actually measured, then writing a method string explaining the calculation. I'm also setting up a per-game suitability module with profile hints, and building a GLB parser that reads the header and JSON chunk to extract mesh, triangle, vertex, material, texture, image, skin, and animation counts, while working out how to compute bounding boxes -- weighing whether to just union the raw accessor min/max values versus properly traversing the node hierarchy and applying each node's transform matrix to get accurate world-space bounds.

Now I'm writing a WAV parser that handles RIFF/WAVE headers, various PCM and float formats, and multiple bit depths, mixing everything down to mono for analysis, while deciding to skip AIFF support and just note it as unmeasured. I'm also confirming the measurement and descriptor functions properly accept a sample rate parameter so they work correctly regardless of the file's native rate, and now starting on the deduplication logic, beginning with exact-match detection.

For near-matches with similar size and triangle count across different packs, I'll flag the later one as a duplicateOf the first ingestion. For audio, I'll match on stem plus tight tolerances on duration and loudness difference to catch re-imports of the same file.

Now I'm laying out the module structure: filters.ts holds rule data from a JSON file, stage-b and stage-c handle the designed pipeline and sampling, index.ts defines the CatalogIndex interface with an in-memory ranked index while sqlite-index.ts is a separate server-only implementation using node:sqlite, tools.ts contains tool definitions and handlers, provider.ts bridges CatalogLibraryProvider to the existing LibraryAsset browse system, and builtin.ts converts the existing sound library manifest and texture templates into the catalog format.

For migration, I'm adding Prisma models including CyrusCatalogEntry, CyrusCatalogReview, and crucially CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun to track a budget ledger across stage-B runs so the hard cap holds across multiple executions. I also want a measurement script that runs stage A over the full dataset and reports coverage by kind/source, gap reasons, and a stage-B cost estimate for remaining items across pricing tiers.

Now I'll move on to writing the vocabulary and text utility modules.

content.thinking:
Now I'm designing the query type for the catalog search, defining fields like text, kinds, game, quality thresholds, licence tiers, tags, categories, and status filters for ranking and retrieval.

For scoring, I'm weighting document fields by importance (title highest, then tags and use-case labels, categories, free tags, description lowest), reusing the existing taxonomy-aware tokenization and synonym expansion so queries match canonical terms, and computing a BM25-style score per matched word using field weight times inverse document frequency. I'm also thinking about coverage requirements — since an LLM-generated query like "sci-fi crate prop" needs most or all words to match for good retrieval, I need to decide how strict the matching threshold should be compared to the existing search's all-words requirement.

Generic words like "prop" or "asset" should be treated as kind hints rather than literal search terms, and I'm excluding queries that match under 60% of terms while scaling partial matches. For final ranking I'm combining normalized text relevance, fit score, and quality multiplicatively so text relevance stays dominant but fit and quality still meaningfully adjust rank, with exact use-case label matches getting an extra boost through field indexing; I also want to collapse duplicate variants into groups, keeping the best hit and counting the rest, and I'm weighing an in-memory inverted index against a SQLite FTS5-backed table for scale.

I'm now sketching the FTS5 schema with weighted fields plus a separate fit table joined on game, the query flow of expanding terms into an OR'd FTS MATCH, pulling top candidates by bm25, then re-ranking in JS using the same scoring function. I'm also planning to isolate the SQLite loading behind a lazy dynamic import since "node:sqlite" could break client bundles in Next, and sketching out the tool schemas for catalog_search and catalog_get with their input validation rules.

I'm designing a compact JSON row format with short keys to minimize token usage per result, aiming for roughly 60 tokens per row so eight rows stay near 500 tokens, with a header carrying total count and a "more" flag, and I'm using a 12-hex-character short id since the collision probability stays acceptably low even at 100k assets.

I also need to handle id ambiguity gracefully—resolving prefixes, lengthening when collisions occur via an index helper that returns the minimal unique prefix—and I'm thinking through plan-based gating so that only asset kinds permitted by the user's tier can be created, returning a clear error with upgrade requirements otherwise.

For tiers, I want a data-driven table defining default access (cc0, cc-by, user-contributed) versus proprietary content gated behind a clearance flag, flagging that as an owner decision to confirm. I also need to extend the mod spec with a libraryRef field so catalog entries can be referenced directly in an asset slot, with the build service resolving that reference back to the actual library content.

content.thinking:
I'm realizing that many of these packs are tilesheets, where individual tiles like tile_0532 are opaque members of a larger sheet — so the meaningful unit to describe is the tileset itself rather than each tile, and coverage for individual tiles is honestly partial at best.

But that reveals a grouping problem: if a folder of a thousand near-identical tiles all get collapsed into one family group, tagging just one representative and copying its description to the rest would be wrong since each tile is visually distinct. I need to distinguish colour-variant families (safe to inherit a shared description) from numbered series with generic stems like "tile" or "sprite" (not safe to inherit) — marking the latter with a "series" prefix so stage B knows not to propagate descriptions, even though it's still cheap to tag each one via contact sheets at 16 per image.

I also realize the grouping key is missing folder awareness: right now tiles with the same stem across different colour folders (like "Tiles (White)/tile_0532" and "Tiles (Black)/tile_0532") should actually belong to the same inheritable variant family since they're just colour variants of the same glyph, so I need the key to strip colour words from both the stem and the folder name while keeping the numeric identifier intact.

Similarly, folder names encoding scale (like "Glow" vs "Glow 2x") should be normalized by stripping scale/size tokens ("2", "x", "2x", "hd", "retina", "large", "small", etc.) so these also group as variants rather than separate families — meanwhile numbered series like different sprite numbers or distinct character colors (playerBlue vs playerRed) should still be treated as genuinely different content, not collapsed.

For the flags pack, I'm considering whether a compact ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code table could be embedded as deterministic zero-token metadata to map codes like "AE" to country names.

For missing categorization like "Laser blue 05" in space-shooter, I'm adding laser/missile/projectile/bullet to the weapons/vfx keyword sets, adding plural-to-singular synonym mapping (missiles→missile), and implementing a generic fallback plural-stripping rule in the canon function so plural keyword variants fold into their singular form automatically, while being careful about recursion issues this could introduce.

For the animal pack, I'm extending the creatures/animals keyword list with more species like giraffe, elephant, lion, tiger, monkey, panda, penguin, hippo, zebra, crocodile, parrot, owl, and snake, since currently the category confidence is too low. I'm also noting that "Roof slant" in the sketch-town set should map to architecture/roofs but lacks a proper useFor tag for modular-building-kit model pieces.

I'm realizing many kind lists built for 3D scenarios should also apply to 2D sprite-based games, so I should add a "sprite" kind to most object categories like modular-building-kit, whole-building, interior-furniture, tool-prop, and kitchen-props. For "Tower defense 133," I'm checking why it scores a suspiciously high 0.9 confidence for architecture/buildings — it looks like the word "tower" is being picked up from both the pack name and filename tokens like "towerDefense_tile133," overweighting that keyword even though this is really a game-prop context rather than pure architecture.

The right fix is to establish a rule: words appearing in both the file content and pack name shouldn't count twice as content signals, so they should be down-weighted to just the pack weight. This means subtracting pack-name words from file content when computing title strength and votes, so for "towerDefense_tile133" the content minus pack words becomes empty, correctly leaving the category opaque. Looking at a few more cases — "Generic color 026" gets a modest 0.43 confidence for items/collectibles which seems honest for partial info, "Lighthouse" needs to be added as a building category, and "Oven outlet" should get a useFor addition for household/appliances. I'm settling on a general precision rule: use primary categories for useFor unless they're empty, then I'll go ahead and make these modifications.

content.thinking:
I'm checking a few entries by hand for correctness, like the "bar_round_small_square" case where the title mapped to "ingot" instead of "bar" due to a synonym clash in the texture taxonomy, flagging it as a title error, and continuing to spot-check items like the coal texture against its category.

Several other entries look shaky too — the marble kit's "fan standing" piece is likely a marble run component mislabeled under appliances, the modular-characters "Black man 6" is really a hair asset with a misleading title, brick-kit pieces are toy bricks miscategorized under walls-floors, the cloud texture sits oddly under nature/terrain instead of sky, and "stone glass blinds" seems to have swapped "window" for "glass" in its title. The road and tower-defense corner pieces look acceptable as-is.

Moving further down, the chalkboard prop got miscategorized under walls-floors just because its name contains "floor" when it should be furniture/decor, the sci-fi woman character file is misplaced under architecture/buildings, "car iron" looks like a title error substituting "silver" with "iron," and a sci-fi megakit decal is also wrongly filed under buildings. Other items like the icon button, disabled box, bottle, washer/dryer, particle circle, plaque, fountain corner, low structure, and conveyor all seem reasonably placed.

Now I'm noticing the war hammer got filed under props/tools when it should be weapons/melee, and there are a few more title-level synonym errors: "frame" being swapped to "panel" and "window" being swapped to "glass." This points to a deeper issue — the taxonomy's synonym-folding (bar→ingot, silver→iron, window→glass, frame→panel) is corrupting titles even when categories are correct, so I need to preserve the raw filename words for titles rather than the canonicalized version, meaning pathTokens should return both the canonical and raw file name. Tallying up, I count 7 category errors and I'm now counting title-only errors separately.

That brings title-only errors to about 7 as well, all traceable to the synonym substitution and fixable with the raw-word approach — giving roughly 93% category precision and 86% title precision before the fix, worth reporting honestly as a single-reviewer hand-check. There's also a stickier issue where "sci_fi" plus a pack name containing "women" got miscategorized into characters instead of architecture, which seems like an upstream tagging problem I can't cleanly fix without weighting pack semantics more heavily — I'll leave that one alone for now and move on to applying the raw-title fix before rerunning.

For the stage-B experiment, I'm planning to sample roughly 150 assets from the partial/none coverage queue, build contact sheets of 16 numbered 128px thumbnails each, manually tag them myself in the stage-B format, and measure the resulting output size — estimating tokens from character counts (acknowledging this is an approximation, not a real tokenizer count) to see what visual tagging would cost per asset. I'll stratify the sample into nine 16-image sheets (144 assets) plus one batch of 40 audio filenames, pulling thumbnails from staging (sprite PNGs, model thumbnails, texture-set previews) via PIL.

import json,random,os
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
ST='/tank/cyrus-library-staging/'
E=[json.loads(l) for l in open('entries.jsonl')]
q=[e for e in E if e['enrichment']['coverage']!='full' and not e.get('duplicateOf') and e.get('thumbnail')]
# one per group
seen=set(); reps=[]
for e in q:
    k=e.get('group') or e['id']
    if k in seen: continue
    seen.add(k); reps.append(e)
random.seed(42)
S=random.sample(reps,144)
cells=[]
for si in range(9):
    im=Image.new('RGB',(512,512),(200,200,200)); d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    for j in range(16):
        e=S[si*16+j]; p=ST+e['thumbnail']
        try:
            t=Image.open(p).convert('RGBA'); t.thumbnail((120,120), Image.NEAREST if max(t.size)<=64 else Image.LANCZOS)
            bg=Image.new('RGBA',(128,128),(200,200,200,255)); bg.alpha_composite(t,((128-t.size[0])//2,(128-t.size[1])//2))
            im.paste(bg.convert('RGB'),((j%4)*128,(j//4)*128))
        except Exception as ex: print('fail',p,ex)
        d.text(((j%4)*128+3,(j//4)*128+2),str(j+1),fill=(255,0,0))
        cells.append({'sheet':si,'i':j+1,'id':e['id'],'path':e['provenance']['path'],'kind':e['kind'],'stageA':{'title':e['title'],'cat':e['categories']['primary'],'cov':e['enrichment']['coverage']}})
    im.save(f'sheets/sheet{si}.png')
json.dump(cells,open('sheets/cells.json','w'),indent=0)
print(len(cells))
EOF

Tiny pixel sprites shown at native size are too small to see, so the sheet builder needs to upscale small sprites using nearest-neighbor scaling to fill each cell instead of just downsizing. entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. content.thinking:
I'm diagnosing why the SQLite upsert for 54k rows took 433 seconds — the FTS delete-by-id was doing a full table scan each time since the id column isn't indexed, causing quadratic behavior. The fix is to align FTS rowids directly with the entry table's rowid so deletes become O(1) lookups instead of scans.

Separately, I notice memory search ranks worse than SQLite because kind hints extracted from the query aren't actually being applied — catalogSearch passes the full allowed kinds list instead of intersecting with the parsed hints, so things like "sound" or "texture" cues get ignored. Fixing that intersection in both memory and SQLite search paths should fix the sprite/texture mis-rankings I'm seeing, and I still need to check why "wooden door" isn't matching — possibly a missing synonym mapping from "wooden" to "wood" in the taxonomy expansion.

The bigger issue is the MIN_WORD_SHARE threshold of 60% for multi-word queries excluding valid partial matches — "health potion" returns zero results because "health" doesn't match any tag even though "potion" clearly should. I'm considering lowering that threshold to 50% but weighting the score by the share squared so partial matches still rank below full matches.

I also notice duplicate rows appearing in results (same title appearing twice, like "Prop crate" or "Night sky hdri 016") — these could be distinct entries from different packs or resolution variants, so the grouping/collapse logic needs to account for that rather than just relying on the group key.

My plan: add kind-hint intersection, apply MIN_WORD_SHARE at 0.5 using share², use SQLite rowid, and collapse title-duplicates in the tool layer with a variant count. I'm also realizing the memory index search is slow (~200-500ms for 54k entries) because it's building field Sets per document on every query instead of precomputing them at upsert time — I need to restructure the doc index to store fields as prebuilt Sets rather than rebuilding them during scoring.

The upsert fix worked, but now the SQLite search is slow, taking seconds. I suspect the issue is the FTS query joining on rid instead of id, losing the index benefit that made it fast before.

Actually, 41s on "ui click" suggests the planner is driving from the entry table and evaluating MATCH per row rather than using FTS as the outer driver. I'm restructuring to pull candidate rowids and scores from FTS first with a limit, then batch-fetch matching entries by rid in chunks with filters applied afterward. There are also remaining ranking issues to look at, like memory results surfacing the wrong kind for texture-related queries.

On digging further, I suspect "texture" might be getting dropped as a stop word during query parsing, which would explain why the kind hint isn't being applied in either the SQLite or memory search paths—so I need to detect kind words from the raw split before stop-word removal happens. There's also an issue where "medieval torch" surfaces Campfire/candle above actual Torch entries, possibly due to synonym mapping or light-category keyword overlap skewing the score.

Looking closer, Campfire likely matches because its useFor label contains "torch" as part of a broader "lamp/torch/light-source prop" description, and since useFor labels are weighted the same as the title (weight 3), that creates false matches when the actual "medieval" tag isn't shared by real torch models. The fix is to split useFor into two fields—keep IDs at weight 3 but lower the label text itself to something like weight 1.5 so broad label overlap doesn't dominate scoring.

For the "wooden door" case, I suspect "wooden" expands to "wood" via term canonicalization, which is pulling in unrelated bridge/log entries tagged "wood". I want to debug this directly against the real entries file—running a quick tsx script over the ~54k entries should only take a few seconds and under a gig of RAM, so I'll write a small untracked debug script and run it on node-2 via devhost rather than loading it on primary.

content.thinking:
I'm puzzled why "sci-fi crate prop" regressed to matching a sci-fi gun model instead of a prop crate — the matching seems to weight partial term overlap oddly, letting a single shared keyword outscore items that actually share both "sci-fi" and "crate" concepts.

Ah, found it: my query tokenizer splits "sci-fi" into two separate words "sci" and "fi", so with "prop" removed, the three terms become sci/fi/crate, and gun titles matching "sci fi" hit 2/3 while crates only hit 1/3, falling below threshold. The fix is to pre-normalize known hyphenated vocabulary like "sci-fi" and "low-poly" into single protected tokens before splitting, so compound tags aren't broken apart during tokenization.

For the "ui click" query, I'm puzzled why "Chimes melodic" and "Party horn" would outrank "Mouse click" despite the latter matching both "ui" via category and "click" via title directly. I'm wondering if query expansion on "click" is pulling in unrelated synonyms like "chime" that inflate scores for the wrong results.

The real problem seems clearer now: if the idf for rare alternative terms is computed on whatever alt actually matched rather than the canonical query term, then rare-word matches can outscore exact common-word matches. The fix is to always compute idf against the first/canonical alt term, not the matched variant, so scoring stays consistent across documents. I'm also noting that the "wooden door" query still surfaces bridge logs first, which needs the same fix.

The dirt road entry seems reasonably categorized under nature/terrain though.

The flag correctly maps to signs, but the rail prop wrongly ends up under buildings, and now I'm looking at the toy car track entry next.

Tallying up: corridor corner from the cave kit fits buildings reasonably, the window light-mask lands correctly in vfx/particles despite a weak title, the decorated table with chairs is an acceptable seating match, but the graveyard kit's detail plate is probably a wrong kitchenware classification, and the metal roof is a marginal fit for buildings. The office corner piece correctly goes to buildings.

I'm counting up clear category errors versus marginal ones to land on roughly 91% precision, noting that many of these mistakes trace back to upstream category labeling issues rather than my own logic. The clothing useFor tag issue seems acceptable given household/clothing overlap in categoriesAny.

Now I need to move on to writing the docs, owner report, and OWNER-ACTIONS file, then commit, merge r2, run the final test pass, and decide whether to rerun the full benchmark given it takes about seven minutes — I'll probably just quote the numbers from the prior run while noting the subsequent ranking fixes.

I'm working through the stage B cost projections at 100k scale. For the staged CC0 dataset, extrapolating the final run's numbers gives roughly 2,020 calls, 3.31M input tokens, and 1.70M output tokens per 100k assets; for audio it's about 614 calls, 1.23M in, 1.21M out. Using current list pricing for Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus, I'm computing the dollar costs across these three scenarios — staged-like mix, worst case, and audio-only — factoring in the roughly 50% batch API discount. ## Cyrus asset catalog (v2)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r14-catalog` (2026-10-10). Code: `lib/cyrus/library/v2/`. Owner report: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/M-catalog-v2.md`. **Library code + one migration file (not applied). No route, no UI, no flag, nothing deployed, no paid model call.**

The metadata, tagging and retrieval layer that lets Cyrus (Claude in the build service) pick the right asset for a situation, at near-zero tokens per asset. It sits on top of the existing unified library (`lib/cyrus/library`, R1): the sound taxonomy, texture taxonomy, plan gate and `browseLibrary` are reused, not replaced.

### 1. CatalogEntry v1 (`entry.ts`, JSON Schema `catalog-entry.v1.schema.json`)
- `id` = sha256 of the bytes (also the dedupe key); referenced everywhere else as `cat:<sha256>`.
- `kind` model | texture-set | texture | sprite | hdri | decal | sound | music; `title` (<=80), `shortDescription` (<=140), `tags` (controlled vocabulary, `vocab.json`) + `freeTags` (<=8), `categories {primary, secondary[<=3]}` (`<domain>/<sub>`; `sound/*` = the sound taxonomy ids, `pixel/*` = the texture-library categories), `useFor` (situation ids, e.g. `gunshot-sound`, `scifi-crate-prop`, `stone-wall-floor-texture`; 66 in `vocab.json`), `style`.
- `quality {score 0-100, version cq-1, method, measured share, checks[]}` (`quality.ts`): weighted pass ratio of the MEASURED checks x (0.4 + 0.6 x measured share); a hard fail (corrupt, silent audio, zero triangles) caps at 20. Model: format, triangles (warn > 50k, fail > 300k), size, materials, real-world scale vs the category; PBR: maps, normal convention, resolution, physical size; 2D: dimensions, power of two, alpha; audio: decode, duration, audible, true peak, silence ratio, sample rate, loudness; all: licence recorded, preview, stage-A confidence.
- `games {game: {fit good|ok|no, reason, notes, transform[]}}` from each game's `AssetProfile` (`fit.ts`). New optional `AssetProfile.catalog` hints (`lib/cyrus/adapters/asset-profile.ts`): accepted kinds (native/convert/none + reasons), style affinity, triangle budgets, texture sizes, audio target. Only Minecraft declares them today: sounds/music `good` (mono Ogg transcode), 16/32/64 px square sprites `good` in pixel style, other 2D `ok`/`no`, glTF / PBR / HDRI / decals `no` (no converter exists; said so in the reason). A game without hints gets no row (= unknown, never assumed good).
- `tech` (tris, vertices, meshes, materials, bounds in metres, rigged, animations; width/height, PBR maps, alpha, tileable, physical size; audio duration, rate, channels, bit depth, peak, true peak, LUFS, silence ratio, loopable heuristic, centroid, transient/sustained), `licence {tier cc0|cc-by|proprietary-nxeon|user-contributed, spdx, sourceUrl, attribution, status}`, `provenance`, `legalClass` (assets3d/manifest.ts), `contributedBy` (opaque), `status` pending-checks|published|held|removed, `flags`, `group` (variant family), `duplicateOf`, `enrichment {by stage-a|stage-b|owner|contributor, confidence, coverage full|partial|none, model, gaps}`. Cross-field rules in `validateCatalogEntry` (cc-by needs attribution, contributions need a contributor and a user class, game-derived / third-party never enter, no hold flag on a published entry).

### 2. Enrichment pipeline
- **Stage A, zero tokens** (`stage-a.ts`, `extract.ts`, `dedupe.ts`): GLB header/JSON-chunk facts (triangles per instance, world bounds through node TRS, skins, animations), WAV decode (8/16/24/32-bit, float, extensible) + the existing sound measures (`lib/cyrus/sound/measure`, `descriptors`, `classify`), PNG IHDR; categories from the source's own category string (alias table) > pack metadata item (Papyszoo `items.json`, Poly Haven / ambientCG API rows) > upstream tags > file-name words > folder words > pack words; synonyms are domain-aware (the sound taxonomy's synonyms never rename a sprite, the texture taxonomy's never rename a sound); titles keep the words as written; Soundminer comma metadata is read; pack cover/preview images are removed; colour/scale variants become one `group`; same file in two packs -> `duplicateOf`.
- **Stage B, cheap AI, only for coverage partial/none** (`stage-b.ts`): one representative per variant group; visual kinds as 512x512 contact sheets of 16 cells (pixel art integer-upscaled, otherwise tiny sprites are unreadable: found in the experiment); audio as text rows (path words + measured features), 40 per call; fixed instruction+vocabulary prefix; replies are one JSON line per cell, Zod-validated, ids outside the vocabulary dropped. Tiers `cheap claude-haiku-4-5 / mid claude-sonnet-5-5 / top claude-opus-5-5` are configuration; prices are inputs. `estimateStageB` = dry-run cost (tokens always, dollars only when prices are given); `runStageB` takes an injected `TaggerClient` and a HARD token budget checked before each call (estimate) and after it (real usage). The migration's `CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun` is the ledger: no paid run without an approved row.
- **Stage C, human spot-check data** (`stage-c.ts`): seeded stratified sample per (kind, stage, coverage), review cards with 5 yes/no questions, precision per stratum with Wilson 95 % intervals; a stratum below the bar (category precision < 0.85, n >= 10) flags its stage's output for hold/rework. Verdicts go to `CyrusCatalogReview`.

### 3. Retrieval (`retrieval.ts`, `sqlite-index.ts`, `tools.ts`)
- `CatalogIndex` interface (upsert, remove, get by id or unique prefix, search, shortId). Implementations: in-memory (pure) and SQLite FTS5 (`node:sqlite`, server-only, FTS rows share the entry rowid). A Postgres/vector backend later implements the same interface.
- Ranking (shared): per query word the best field it hits (title 3.5, situation ids 3, tags 2.5, categories 2, free tags 1, description 1, situation labels 0.75) x idf of the typed word, >= 50 % of words must hit, scaled by share squared; kind words in the query ("sound", "texture", "prop") narrow the kinds; compounds (`sci fi`, `low poly`) are one term; then `rank = text x (0.6 + 0.4 x fit) x (0.75 + 0.25 x quality/100)`, fit good 1 / ok 0.6 / unknown 0.35, `no` excluded. Filters: status published only, near-duplicates out, kind, licence tier, min quality, tags, category, situation; one row per variant group and per (kind, title).
- **Tool contract** for the build service (`CATALOG_TOOLS`, `handleCatalogTool`): `catalog_search(query, kind?, game?, minQuality=40, limit<=8)` -> `{n, game, rows:[{id "c:<12+ hex>", t, d, k, tags<=5, fit, q, tris|sec|px, variants?}]}`, hard-capped at 3,800 chars (~1k tokens; measured 490-620 tokens for 8 rows); `catalog_get(id)` -> `{ref "cat:<sha256>", title, description, category, style, tags, situations, quality + failed checks, fit for the project's game with notes and transforms, tech, licence}`. Gates on every call: `canAsset(plan, gateKindOf(kind), "create")` (sound = Saka+, visual = top plan, free/Katara nothing, unknown plan fails closed), `PLAN_TIERS` (owner decision), proprietary tier only when the host passes `proprietaryCleared` (same rule as `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED`); an entry the caller may not use answers `not_found`.
- **ModSpec**: asset slots gained optional `libraryRef: "cat:<sha256>"`, only valid with `source: "library"` (error otherwise; warning when a library slot has none). `useSoundFromLibrary` / `useTextureFromLibrary` now set it (texture only when the item is used as drawn). `resolveLibrarySlot(slot, ctx)` is what the build service runs per library slot: exists, published, kind matches, plan gate, tier, game fit not `no`, returns the transforms to apply.
- `pipeline.ts`: `CatalogStore` interface (host implements it on the new tables), `ingestRows`, `contribute` (community auto-contribution: always pending-checks -> strict filters), `builtinRows` (the 514 owner sounds + 281 Cyrus templates as entries), `catalogProvider` / `entryAsLibraryAsset` (v2 entries inside the existing `browseLibrary`).

### 4. Content filters (`filters.ts`, `filter-rules.json`)
`ContentFilter` interface (async, so a classifier can plug in later; a throwing filter holds = fail closed). First deterministic ruleset: eligibility (`libraryEligible`: uploads, imports, templates and anything with `derivedFrom` are removed from the community path), adult terms (reject), extremist terms (reject community / hold packs), real firearm model names (hold community / flag packs), trademark STUB list (hold community; flag for packs and for console glyphs in input-prompt packs), mature violence (flag), drugs (hold/flag), pack preview images (reject), quality hard fail (hold). Held never auto-publishes.

### 5. Measured (read-only copy of the staged catalog, 51,391 rows, + 1,953 SFX file names from the partial upload, + 795 built-ins)
Stage A alone: 54.7 % full / 23.2 % partial / 22.1 % none on the staged CC0 rows (models 98.7 % full, HDRIs and decals 100 %, PBR sets 81 %, sprites 41.6 %, plain textures 18 %); SFX names 76.9 % full before any audio is measured; built-ins 94.5 %. Hand check of 100 random `full` entries: 91 right category, 2 marginal, 7 wrong (mostly upstream pack categories, e.g. toy-brick plates as kitchenware). Stage-B queue after variant collapse: 16,601 cells for 22,865 assets, 1,038 sheet calls, about 1.70 M input + 0.88 M output tokens (estimator). Index build at 54k entries: memory 1.8 s, SQLite 5.3 s; queries 2-180 ms on node-2.

### 6. Tests, scripts, migration
`test/cyrus-catalog-v2.test.ts` (39 tests: schema, tokenising, GLB/WAV/PNG facts on in-memory fixtures, stage A on real rows and synthesised audio, quality, fit, dedupe, filters, both indexes, tools + gates, ModSpec refs, stage B with a fake client and the budget stop, stage C, built-ins, and the golden test over 200 real staged rows: `test/fixtures/cyrus-catalog/`, regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/catalog-golden.ts`). `scripts/cyrus/catalog-stage-a.ts` = the coverage/cost/bench measurement; `scripts/cyrus/catalog-schema.ts` writes the JSON Schema. Migration: `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-catalog-v2.sql` (NOT applied; additive: `CyrusCatalogEntry`, `CyrusCatalogReview`, `CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun`, no FKs).

- `tech` (tris, vertices, meshes, materials, bounds in metres, rigged, animations; width/height, PBR maps, alpha, tileable, physical size; audio duration, rate, channels, bit depth, peak, true peak, LUFS, silence ratio, loopable heuristic, centroid, transient/sustained), `licence {tier cc0|cc-by|proprietary-nxeon|user-contributed, spdx, sourceUrl, attribution, status}`, `provenance`, `legalClass` (assets3d/manifest.ts), `contributedBy` (opaque), `status` pending-checks|published|held|removed, `flags`, `group` (variant family), `duplicateOf`, `enrichment {by stage-a|stage-b|owner|contributor, confidence, coverage full|partial|none, model, gaps}`. Cross-field rules in `validateCatalogEntry` (cc-by needs attribution, contributions need a contributor and a user class, game-derived / third-party never enter, no hold flag on a published entry).

### 2. Enrichment pipeline
- **Stage A, zero tokens** (`stage-a.ts`, `extract.ts`, `dedupe.ts`): GLB header/JSON-chunk facts (triangles per instance, world bounds through node TRS, skins, animations), WAV decode (8/16/24/32-bit, float, extensible) + the existing sound measures (`lib/cyrus/sound/measure`, `descriptors`, `classify`), PNG IHDR; categories from the source's own category string (alias table) > pack metadata item (Papyszoo `items.json`, Poly Haven / ambientCG API rows) > upstream tags > file-name words > folder words > pack words; synonyms are domain-aware (the sound taxonomy's synonyms never rename a sprite, the texture taxonomy's never rename a sound); titles keep the words as written; Soundminer comma metadata is read; pack cover/preview images are removed; colour/scale variants become one `group`; same file in two packs -> `duplicateOf`.
- **Stage B, cheap AI, only for coverage partial/none** (`stage-b.ts`): one representative per variant group; visual kinds as 512x512 contact sheets of 16 cells (pixel art integer-upscaled, otherwise tiny sprites are unreadable: found in the experiment); audio as text rows (path words + measured features), 40 per call; fixed instruction+vocabulary prefix; replies are one JSON line per cell, Zod-validated, ids outside the vocabulary dropped. Tiers `cheap claude-haiku-4-5 / mid claude-sonnet-5-5 / top claude-opus-5-5` are configuration; prices are inputs. `estimateStageB` = dry-run cost (tokens always, dollars only when prices are given); `runStageB` takes an injected `TaggerClient` and a HARD token budget checked before each call (estimate) and after it (real usage). The migration's `CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun` is the ledger: no paid run without an approved row.
- **Stage C, human spot-check data** (`stage-c.ts`): seeded stratified sample per (kind, stage, coverage), review cards with 5 yes/no questions, precision per stratum with Wilson 95 % intervals; a stratum below the bar (category precision < 0.85, n >= 10) flags its stage's output for hold/rework. Verdicts go to `CyrusCatalogReview`.

### 3. Retrieval (`retrieval.ts`, `sqlite-index.ts`, `tools.ts`)
- `CatalogIndex` interface (upsert, remove, get by id or unique prefix, search, shortId). Implementations: in-memory (pure) and SQLite FTS5 (`node:sqlite`, server-only, FTS rows share the entry rowid). A Postgres/vector backend later implements the same interface.
- Ranking (shared): per query word the best field it hits (title 3.5, situation ids 3, tags 2.5, categories 2, free tags 1, description 1, situation labels 0.75) x idf of the typed word, >= 50 % of words must hit, scaled by share squared; kind words in the query ("sound", "texture", "prop") narrow the kinds; compounds (`sci fi`, `low poly`) are one term; then `rank = text x (0.6 + 0.4 x fit) x (0.75 + 0.25 x quality/100)`, fit good 1 / ok 0.6 / unknown 0.35, `no` excluded. Filters: status published only, near-duplicates out, kind, licence tier, min quality, tags, category, situation; one row per variant group and per (kind, title).
- **Tool contract** for the build service (`CATALOG_TOOLS`, `handleCatalogTool`): `catalog_search(query, kind?, game?, minQuality=40, limit<=8)` -> `{n, game, rows:[{id "c:<12+ hex>", t, d, k, tags<=5, fit, q, tris|sec|px, variants?}]}`, hard-capped at 3,800 chars (~1k tokens; measured 490-620 tokens for 8 rows); `catalog_get(id)` -> `{ref "cat:<sha256>", title, description, category, style, tags, situations, quality + failed checks, fit for the project's game with notes and transforms, tech, licence}`. Gates on every call: `canAsset(plan, gateKindOf(kind), "create")` (sound = Saka+, visual = top plan, free/Katara nothing, unknown plan fails closed), `PLAN_TIERS` (owner decision), proprietary tier only when the host passes `proprietaryCleared` (same rule as `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED`); an entry the caller may not use answers `not_found`.
- **ModSpec**: asset slots gained optional `libraryRef: "cat:<sha256>"`, only valid with `source: "library"` (error otherwise; warning when a library slot has none). `useSoundFromLibrary` / `useTextureFromLibrary` now set it (texture only when the item is used as drawn). `resolveLibrarySlot(slot, ctx)` is what the build service runs per library slot: exists, published, kind matches, plan gate, tier, game fit not `no`, returns the transforms to apply.
- `pipeline.ts`: `CatalogStore` interface (host implements it on the new tables), `ingestRows`, `contribute` (community auto-contribution: always pending-checks -> strict filters), `builtinRows` (the 514 owner sounds + 281 Cyrus templates as entries), `catalogProvider` / `entryAsLibraryAsset` (v2 entries inside the existing `browseLibrary`).

### 4. Content filters (`filters.ts`, `filter-rules.json`)
`ContentFilter` interface (async, so a classifier can plug in later; a throwing filter holds = fail closed). First deterministic ruleset: eligibility (`libraryEligible`: uploads, imports, templates and anything with `derivedFrom` are removed from the community path), adult terms (reject), extremist terms (reject community / hold packs), real firearm model names (hold community / flag packs), trademark STUB list (hold community; flag for packs and for console glyphs in input-prompt packs), mature violence (flag), drugs (hold/flag), pack preview images (reject), quality hard fail (hold). Held never auto-publishes.

### 5. Measured (read-only copy of the staged catalog, 51,391 rows, + 1,953 SFX file names from the partial upload, + 795 built-ins)
Stage A alone: 54.7 % full / 23.2 % partial / 22.1 % none on the staged CC0 rows (models 98.7 % full, HDRIs and decals 100 %, PBR sets 81 %, sprites 41.6 %, plain textures 18 %); SFX names 76.9 % full before any audio is measured; built-ins 94.5 %. Hand check of 100 random `full` entries: 91 right category, 2 marginal, 7 wrong (mostly upstream pack categories, e.g. toy-brick plates as kitchenware). Stage-B queue after variant collapse: 16,601 cells for 22,865 assets, 1,038 sheet calls, about 1.70 M input + 0.88 M output tokens (estimator). Index build at 54k entries: memory 1.8 s, SQLite 5.3 s; queries 2-180 ms on node-2.

### 6. Tests, scripts, migration
`test/cyrus-catalog-v2.test.ts` (39 tests: schema, tokenising, GLB/WAV/PNG facts on in-memory fixtures, stage A on real rows and synthesised audio, quality, fit, dedupe, filters, both indexes, tools + gates, ModSpec refs, stage B with a fake client and the budget stop, stage C, built-ins, and the golden test over 200 real staged rows: `test/fixtures/cyrus-catalog/`, regenerate with `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/catalog-golden.ts`). `scripts/cyrus/catalog-stage-a.ts` = the coverage/cost/bench measurement; `scripts/cyrus/catalog-schema.ts` writes the JSON Schema. Migration: `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-catalog-v2.sql` (NOT applied; additive: `CyrusCatalogEntry`, `CyrusCatalogReview`, `CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun`, no FKs).

# M. Cyrus asset catalog v2 (owner report, 2026-10-10)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r14-catalog` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r14`, merged with the latest `feature/cyrus-r2`). Code `lib/cyrus/library/v2/`, docs "Cyrus asset catalog (v2)". Nothing deployed, no migration run, no flag, no paid model call.

## What each asset now carries (CatalogEntry v1)
Content-hash id (`cat:<sha256>` everywhere), kind (model, PBR set, texture, sprite, HDRI, decal, sound, music), title, description (<=140 chars), controlled tags + up to 8 free tags, one primary + up to 3 secondary categories (the existing sound and texture taxonomies are reused inside it), **situations** ("gunshot sound", "sci-fi crate prop", "stone wall floor texture": 66 of them), style, a **quality score 0-100 with every check listed** (only measured checks count; a corrupt/silent/zero-triangle file is capped at 20), **fit per game** (good/ok/no + reason + budget notes + what Cyrus must do to it, read from each game's asset profile), technical facts (triangles, size in metres, rig/animations, maps, resolution; audio length, sample rate, channels, peak, loudness, silence, loop hint), licence tier (CC0, CC-BY, Nxeon-owned, user-contributed), provenance, legal class, opaque contributor, status (pending, published, held, removed).

## Measured: how much needs no AI at all (stage A)
Read-only copy of the staged catalog (51,391 rows at copy time), plus 1,953 file names from the partial SFX upload and the 795 existing built-ins:

| Set | Fully described by stage A |
|---|---|
| 3D models (10,018) | **98.7 %** |
| HDRIs (433), decals (127) | 100 % |
| PBR texture sets (2,079) | 81 % |
| Sprites (38,056) | 41.6 % (mostly Kenney tiles named `tile_0113.png`) |
| Plain textures (678) | 18 % |
| **All staged CC0** | **54.7 % full, 23.2 % partial, 22.1 % none** |
| SFX names only (audio not yet measurable: zip still uploading) | 76.9 % |
| Built-ins (514 owner sounds, 281 Cyrus textures) | 94.5 % |

Precision: I hand-checked 100 random "full" entries: 91 right, 2 marginal, 7 wrong category (mostly the upstream pack's own labels, e.g. toy-brick "plates" filed as kitchenware). 283 pack cover/preview images were found and removed automatically.

## Cost to tag the rest (stage B)
Measured on my own tagging of 144 queued images (9 contact sheets of 16) and 40 sound names: replies average 186 characters per asset; 74 % of images and 93 % of sound names reached usable confidence (the rest are tile fragments no one can name from a thumbnail). The estimator turns the staged queue into 1,038 calls, about **1.70 M input + 0.88 M output tokens** for 22,865 assets (one cell per colour/scale variant family).

Scaled linearly to **100k assets with the same mix: about 3.3 M input + 1.7 M output tokens.** Worst case (every asset needs AI, no families): about 10.2 M input + 5.3 M output. Cost = input/1M x input price + output/1M x output price; **the price per token is an input to the estimator.** With the list prices in the Claude API reference I have (cached 2026-09-25, verify before any run):

| Tier | Typical 100k | Worst case 100k |
|---|---|---|
| cheap (Haiku 4.5, $1/$5 per MTok) | ~$12 | ~$37 |
| mid (Sonnet 5.5, $2/$10) | ~$24 | ~$73 |
| top (Opus 5.5, $4/$20) | ~$47 | ~$147 |

The Batch API halves these. Assumptions: 3.6 characters per token, image tokens = width x height / 750, ~950-token fixed prefix per call (prompt caching not assumed). None of these were re-measured with the real token counter (no key, no spend).

## Retrieval
`catalog_search` returns at most 8 compact rows, capped at ~1k tokens (measured 490-620 tokens). `catalog_get` returns the `ref` that goes into a ModSpec asset slot (`source: "library"`, new `libraryRef`). Every call applies the plan gate (sounds Saka+, visuals top plan, free/Katara nothing), the licence tiers per plan, and the proprietary-library clearance. Local index: memory or SQLite full-text, 54k entries built in 2-5 s, queries 2-180 ms.

## Community library
Assets made in Cyrus enter as pending, then deterministic filters: adult terms removed; real-gun model names, trademarks (stub list), extremist and drug terms held for you; gore flagged; uploads/imports/derived work never auto-contributed.

## Owner decisions
1. Licence tiers per plan (`PLAN_TIERS`): today Saka and top plan may use CC0, CC-BY, community and (once cleared) the proprietary library.
2. Clear the proprietary SFX library per pack (licence text per pack folder) before customer builds use it; real-gun pack names (FN Five-seveN, Mini Uzi...) are flagged, not held, for your own library: keep or rename titles?
3. Which tier for stage B, and a budget cap (suggest a 500-asset dry run first, then cheap tier on sprites only).
4. Extend the trademark list (stub) and confirm "hold, owner reviews" for community assets named after real guns.
5. Asset profiles for the next games (only Minecraft declares catalog hints; every 3D asset is honestly "no" for Minecraft until a glTF converter exists).
6. Accept a 2-letter country-code table for the 457 flag sprites (free, zero tokens).

## Unverified
Token counts (estimated from characters and the published image formula, not counted); cheap/mid-tier tagging accuracy (only my own tagging was measured); audio features of the new SFX library (not extractable until the upload completes); loopable is a heuristic; Postgres search backend not built (interface only); no UI.

# M. Cyrus asset catalog v2 (owner report, 2026-10-10)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r14-catalog` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r14`, merged with the latest `feature/cyrus-r2`). Code `lib/cyrus/library/v2/`, docs "Cyrus asset catalog (v2)". Nothing deployed, no migration run, no flag, no paid model call.

## What each asset now carries (CatalogEntry v1)
Content-hash id (`cat:<sha256>` everywhere), kind (model, PBR set, texture, sprite, HDRI, decal, sound, music), title, description (<=140 chars), controlled tags + up to 8 free tags, one primary + up to 3 secondary categories (the existing sound and texture taxonomies are reused inside it), **situations** ("gunshot sound", "sci-fi crate prop", "stone wall floor texture": 66 of them), style, a **quality score 0-100 with every check listed** (only measured checks count; a corrupt/silent/zero-triangle file is capped at 20), **fit per game** (good/ok/no + reason + budget notes + what Cyrus must do to it, read from each game's asset profile), technical facts (triangles, size in metres, rig/animations, maps, resolution; audio length, sample rate, channels, peak, loudness, silence, loop hint), licence tier (CC0, CC-BY, Nxeon-owned, user-contributed), provenance, legal class, opaque contributor, status (pending, published, held, removed).

## Measured: how much needs no AI at all (stage A)
Read-only copy of the staged catalog (51,391 rows at copy time), plus 1,953 file names from the partial SFX upload and the 795 existing built-ins:

| Set | Fully described by stage A |
|---|---|
| 3D models (10,018) | **98.7 %** |
| HDRIs (433), decals (127) | 100 % |
| PBR texture sets (2,079) | 81 % |
| Sprites (38,056) | 41.6 % (mostly Kenney tiles named `tile_0113.png`) |
| Plain textures (678) | 18 % |
| **All staged CC0** | **54.7 % full, 23.2 % partial, 22.1 % none** |
| SFX names only (audio not yet measurable: zip still uploading) | 76.9 % |
| Built-ins (514 owner sounds, 281 Cyrus textures) | 94.5 % |

Precision: I hand-checked 100 random "full" entries: 91 right, 2 marginal, 7 wrong category (mostly the upstream pack's own labels, e.g. toy-brick "plates" filed as kitchenware). 283 pack cover/preview images were found and removed automatically.

## Cost to tag the rest (stage B)
Measured on my own tagging of 144 queued images (9 contact sheets of 16) and 40 sound names: replies average 186 characters per asset; 74 % of images and 93 % of sound names reached usable confidence (the rest are tile fragments no one can name from a thumbnail). The estimator turns the staged queue into 1,038 calls, about **1.70 M input + 0.88 M output tokens** for 22,865 assets (one cell per colour/scale variant family).

Scaled linearly to **100k assets with the same mix: about 3.3 M input + 1.7 M output tokens.** Worst case (every asset needs AI, no families): about 10.2 M input + 5.3 M output. Cost = input/1M x input price + output/1M x output price; **the price per token is an input to the estimator.** With the list prices in the Claude API reference I have (cached 2026-09-25, verify before any run):

| Tier | Typical 100k | Worst case 100k |
|---|---|---|
| cheap (Haiku 4.5, $1/$5 per MTok) | ~$12 | ~$37 |
| mid (Sonnet 5.5, $2/$10) | ~$24 | ~$73 |
| top (Opus 5.5, $4/$20) | ~$47 | ~$147 |

The Batch API halves these. Assumptions: 3.6 characters per token, image tokens = width x height / 750, ~950-token fixed prefix per call (prompt caching not assumed). None of these were re-measured with the real token counter (no key, no spend).

## Retrieval
`catalog_search` returns at most 8 compact rows, capped at ~1k tokens (measured 490-620 tokens). `catalog_get` returns the `ref` that goes into a ModSpec asset slot (`source: "library"`, new `libraryRef`). Every call applies the plan gate (sounds Saka+, visuals top plan, free/Katara nothing), the licence tiers per plan, and the proprietary-library clearance. Local index: memory or SQLite full-text, 54k entries built in 2-5 s, queries 2-180 ms.

## Community library
Assets made in Cyrus enter as pending, then deterministic filters: adult terms removed; real-gun model names, trademarks (stub list), extremist and drug terms held for you; gore flagged; uploads/imports/derived work never auto-contributed.

## Owner decisions
1. Licence tiers per plan (`PLAN_TIERS`): today Saka and top plan may use CC0, CC-BY, community and (once cleared) the proprietary library.
2. Clear the proprietary SFX library per pack (licence text per pack folder) before customer builds use it; real-gun pack names (FN Five-seveN, Mini Uzi...) are flagged, not held, for your own library: keep or rename titles?
3. Which tier for stage B, and a budget cap (suggest a 500-asset dry run first, then cheap tier on sprites only).
4. Extend the trademark list (stub) and confirm "hold, owner reviews" for community assets named after real guns.
5. Asset profiles for the next games (only Minecraft declares catalog hints; every 3D asset is honestly "no" for Minecraft until a glTF converter exists).
6. Accept a 2-letter country-code table for the 457 flag sprites (free, zero tokens).

## Unverified
Token counts (estimated from characters and the published image formula, not counted); cheap/mid-tier tagging accuracy (only my own tagging was measured); audio features of the new SFX library (not extractable until the upload completes); loopable is a heuristic; Postgres search backend not built (interface only); no UI.
